title.point: We should follow God’s commandments and the rules and regulations set before us.

lastWeekReview.title: The Destruction of Jericho
bullets: The children of Israel had crossed the Jordan and came to their first city — the strong, walled city of JERICHO.
The king locked the GATES tight, trusting his high walls to keep God’s people out.
God gave Joshua VERY unusual instructions: march around the city once a day for six days, carrying the ark — and stay SILENT.
On the SEVENTH day they marched around seven times, the priests blew the trumpets, and the people SHOUTED.
The mighty walls FELL down flat, and the city was taken — only the one true God could do that!
Only Rahab and her household were SAVED, just as the two spies had promised.
God’s word is always true — even when His instructions don’t make sense, we can trust and obey!
lastWeekReview.discussion: Did you obey an older one this week even when their instruction didn’t make sense to you — and later see it was for your good? Share how it went!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “Trust in Jehovah with all your heart, / And do not rely on your own understanding.” — Proverbs 3:5-6

kidsContent.text: When Everyone Did His Own Thing
After Jericho fell, the children of Israel enjoyed many years of PEACE. They had God as their King, and they loved Him.

But the people changed. They turned their backs on God and abandoned Him! Instead of loving God, they loved idols — things made of wood and stone. Everyone did what was right in his OWN eyes (Judges 17:6).
When everyone follows their own ideas instead of God, things get rotten and out of order. So God raised up JUDGES to keep His people in line and correct what was wrong.
A judge is like an arbitrator — someone who helps everyone agree on a fair solution, a lot like a school principal. Are judges bad for us? No — they are for our GOOD!
🌟 If everyone followed God’s commandments, we wouldn’t need judges at all. Because people don’t, God gives us judges to keep things fair and in order — for our good!

image.caption: Israel in the land during the time of the judges

kidsContent.text: Even now that you are children, God has placed many “judges” around you for your benefit. Your mom might be a “judge” when two siblings argue. A serving one might be a “judge” to help settle a matter between children.

Children and even grownups around us sometimes do what the Israelites did — doing what THEY think is right instead of following God’s commandments. But God cares for us by setting “judges” over us — parents, serving ones, teachers, and principals.
We want to be those who ACCEPT God’s arrangement and receive the help and advice of these “judges,” so we can follow God’s commandments and the rules and regulations around us.
🌟 Go home today thanking God for His arrangement! Every “judge” in your life was placed by God to guide you — let’s be those who follow the rules and regulations set for us!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, when a “judge” God has placed over you — a parent, teacher, serving one, or principal — corrects you or settles a matter, receive it gladly. Follow God’s commandments and the rules and regulations set before you, instead of doing what is right in your own eyes.

memoryVerse.text: Hallelujah! / Blessed is the man who fears Jehovah, / Who delights greatly in His commandments.
memoryVerse.application: We are blessed and truly happy when we love God and keep His commandments — and the rules our parents and teachers set for us! Instead of doing whatever is right in our own eyes, we get to delight in obeying God and the “judges” He has placed around us.

activity.title: ⚖️ The Fair Judge — Order out of Chaos

parts.text: Materials: A “judge’s” badge or hat, a small bell or gavel (a wooden spoon works!), a bin of shared toys or blocks, and index cards with simple “disputes” written on them.
Setup: Divide the kids into small groups. Tell them: for Round 1 there are NO rules and no judge — everyone just does what is right in their own eyes.

Round 1 — Everyone’s Own Way: Give each group one bin of toys/blocks to build with, but no rules for sharing or taking turns. Watch the chaos: grabbing, arguing, nothing gets built. Pause and ask — how did that feel?

Round 2 — Appoint a Judge: Each group picks one “judge” (badge + gavel). Now hand a group a dispute card (“Two kids want the same red block”). The judge listens to both sides and decides a fair solution.
Round 3 — Build in Order: With the judge keeping order and everyone following the rules, groups build their tower again. Notice how much more gets done when everyone follows the rules and the judge!

📖 Connection: When everyone did what was right in his own eyes, Israel became rotten and needed judges. God gives us “judges” — parents, serving ones, principals — for our good, so we can follow His commandments and live in order!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: A classroom during art time. The teacher steps out for a moment, and the room is loud and messy. Three kids — Max, Lily, and Sam — are at one table.
For a while things were peaceful in the classroom. But the moment the teacher stepped out, everyone started doing whatever was right in their own eyes.
Teacher’s gone! I’m taking ALL the markers — I don’t care about turns!
Hey, those are mine! Give them back! I was using the blue one!
Who needs rules anyway? I’m going to paint on the desk — nobody can stop me!

Soon the whole table was a mess. Paint everywhere, no one sharing, everyone grabbing. It was just like Israel long ago — everyone did what was right in his own eyes, and everything became rotten and out of order.
This is TERRIBLE! Nobody is being fair. My picture is ruined and I didn’t even get a turn!
The teacher walks back in and sees the chaos. She rings a little bell for quiet.
Children, when everyone does only what THEY want, no one is happy. That is exactly why we need someone to help keep things fair — a judge.
A judge? Like… the boss of the markers?
A judge is someone who helps everyone agree on what is fair. God placed judges over Israel for their good — and He placed teachers and parents over you for YOUR good.
The teacher helped them clean up and set fair turns for the markers. In a few minutes, the noisy, unhappy table became peaceful again.
Wow — everyone got a turn, and my picture actually turned out nice. Following the rules is way better than the mess!
So the teacher wasn’t being mean… she was helping us. The rules were for our good all along.
We’ll follow God’s commandments and the rules and regulations set for us — the “judges” God gives us are for our good!

description.text: Setup: One child is the “Judge” at the far wall with their back to the group. Everyone else lines up at the start, trying to reach the Judge.
Rules: When the Judge faces away and calls “Follow the rules!”, players move forward. When the Judge turns around, everyone must FREEZE — moving after the freeze is breaking the rule.
Out: Anyone the Judge catches moving after the freeze goes back to the start line — the rule is the rule, even when it’s hard!
Win: The first player to reach the Judge while keeping the rules becomes the next Judge.
📖 Connection: When everyone did his own thing, Israel fell into chaos. Following the judge and the rules keeps the game — and our lives — fair and in order!
Materials: Open space, a start line and a finish wall
Setup: Everyone stands in an open space. One leader is the “Judge” who calls out the moves.
Rules: This is like “Simon Says.” Only do the move when the Judge says “Judge says…” first. Do it without those words, and you’ve broken the rule.
Out: If you move when the Judge did NOT say “Judge says,” or you ignore a real command, do 5 jumping jacks and rejoin.
Twist: Speed up the calls so players must pay close attention and keep following the one in charge — not just doing their own thing.
📖 Connection: A good judge keeps everyone in order. We stay happy and safe when we listen to the “judges” God places over us and follow the rules!
Materials: Open space, no equipment needed
Split the kids into two teams, each running a simple obstacle relay (run to the cone, hop back, tag the next runner).
Choose one child to be the “Referee” (judge). The Referee watches for anyone who cuts corners, skips a step, or runs out of turn.
Rule: If a runner breaks a rule, the Referee calls it and that runner redoes their turn fairly — the game only works when everyone follows the rules.
Finish: Gather together and thank God that He gives us “judges” — parents, serving ones, and teachers — to keep things fair and for our good.
Materials: Cones or markers, open outdoor space

outdoor.tip: ⚖️ The lesson is order and care: when everyone does what is right in his own eyes, things fall apart. Help the kids feel that the “judges” God places around them — parents, serving ones, teachers, principals — are a gift for their good, not a punishment.
